summary: Stillwood March re-authored around a 450 m camp-to-fort anchor distance, editable landmark kits, deterministic biome/route/scatter Resources, editor preview, shared map geometry and incremental local navigation.
scope: Environmental/region authoring only. The current movement, camera zooms, combat, HUD layout, spell tuning, controls, progression and renderer are preserved.

scale.travel_caveat: Arithmetic only; excludes acceleration, obstacles, combat, transformation and stamina exhaustion.

blocked_area.generated_contribution: Not measured without running the generator. map_data().blocked_area_estimate_m2 includes procedural tree/prop footprints at runtime.
blocked_area.caveat: Raw sums include overlaps and boundary strips outside the region. Not an exact collision union or net walkable-area calculation.

inventory_note: Relative to this overhaul, not all existing uncommitted project work. Existing .uid identities are preserved. Other dirty/untracked files predate this pass and were not reset.
runtime_connected: ForestCamp uses the same seeded placement pipeline for runtime and explicit editor previews. Opening/reopening scenes never triggers full-region generation. Preview instantiates only a bounded local window; authored landmarks remain visible. Preview suppresses enemies, player controls, HUD, audio and gameplay effects.
OverworldDefinition owns typed routes/biomes/scatter. RegionLandmark scene transforms own landmark/map/discovery locations; encounter markers and footprint/access reservations are editable.
Six blended soil/vegetation biomes; broadleaf, conifer and dead trees; neighbour-aware seamless ground patches; joined road shoulders/centres; deterministic route-side scenery reserved before trees.

Ten landmark scene kits: ruined chapel with broken apse, rootbound grave clusters, pool, waystone, split oak, bridge crossing, watchtower, Pilgrim's Rest, terraced quarry and fort gate/courtyard/roofless hall.
Continuous connected boundary formations replace the old clearing boundaries and previous perimeter rock ring. Collisions stay loaded while decorative processing is culled.

Ground-only obstacles allow Raven flight but block invalid human landing. Substantial walls and boundary cliffs block flight. Upper architectural artwork and tree canopies retain reveal without affecting collisions.
Six existing Sentinel encounters reuse the previous regional spatial scale and unchanged combat/AI archetype. No boss is added.

Local 64x64 navigation grids build incrementally, up to 256 probes per physics frame across pending work. Up to eight ready and eight pending windows; pending/invalid paths return empty for retry. Player window prewarms every 0.5s; rebuild invalidates caches.

Map derives biome colours, roads, water/solid/floor polygons, canopy aggregates and landmark coordinates from built world data. Distant woodland LOD and prioritised label placement improve legibility. Map redraw is input-driven while paused.
Existing full-screen M map, wheel zoom, panning, markers, beacons, 2-second arrival fade, transitions, vignette and discovery rules remain. Fort Greywatch is known initially.
Particle and light budgets remain unchanged: 256 ambient plus 1792 transient particles, eight temporary lights. No new emitters or persistent lights are added by this pass.
authoring: Open scenes/forest_camp.tscn. Move/edit existing scene instances under Actors/Landmarks, or edit their source scenes.
Edit routes, biome profiles and scatter in data/stillwood_region.tres. Coordinates/widths use metres; scene transforms use metres times 128.

On the camp root, under Editor Preview, set Preview Center Metres and Preview Half Extent Metres, then toggle Rebuild Region Preview. Default window is 64x64 m plus margins; half-extent is capped at 64 m. Repeated requests are coalesced. Only ownerless generated roots are replaced; manual nodes and landmark instances remain.
Keep manual edits outside generated terrain/dressing roots. Generated nodes are not scene-owned or baked into the scene.
Reload the running scene after authoring changes to refresh the HUD map snapshot. Runtime rebuild already invalidates navigation windows.
compatibility: Reported route Array type errors are resolved: generation iterates RegionRouteDefinition; map_data explicitly creates separate Array[Dictionary] presentation records.
Original player/shrine/fire/camp-tree positions and camp proportions remain unchanged.
Movement Resource, Raven Resource and player scene hashes match the pre-pass baseline. No changes to speed, acceleration, stamina or zoom.
No shared .tres mutation during generation. Per-enemy display-name edits use duplicated definitions.
No fake distant fort projection, disconnected level transitions, new enemy archetype, boss, loot, progression, fast travel or persistence.

performed: Source-coordinate route corridor and encounter footprint clearance inspection
runtime_unverified: All human/Raven paths, water landings, bridge/gate clearance and boundaries
Canopy/architecture reveal, equipment ordering and Raven above-canopy rendering
Pause, shrine rest, death, reload and repeated editor regeneration
CPU/GPU performance and generation latency at widest Raven zoom
limits: No claim that static inspection proves Godot startup or engine parsing.
Blocked-area values are approximate source footprint sums, not measured net walkable terrain.
Scenery candidates can be skipped for clearance; density needs play review.
Local grids do not provide full-region long-distance AI routing; out-of-window paths idle/retry.
Only shallow modular fort exploration is included, not a finished legacy dungeon.

editor_recovery.finding: The restored forest scene's @tool _ready() automatically generated the full region. This was a likely contributor to the reopening stall; no crash log confirmed a specific engine failure.
changes: Bounded explicit preview to a local window
Preserved deterministic runtime placement by keeping off-window reservations/random consumption
editor_recovery.verification: User reported the editor was accessible again. Source inspection only for these changes; no engine import, runtime or automated tests run.
